title: Solar panels
subtitle: how sunlight becomes power
facts: Solar panels are photovoltaic: they turn light directly into electricity, with no moving parts.
Each silicon cell has two differently doped layers (n-type and p-type) that meet at a p-n junction.
Light arrives as photons; an absorbed photon can free an electron from its atom in the silicon.
The junction's built-in electric field pushes the freed electrons one way, so they flow out through the cell's contacts into the circuit as current.
Typical home panels convert about 20% of the sunlight that hits them into electricity (commonly around 18 to 23%).
